title: There is no shame in earning a living
literal_meaning: Feed yourself; there is no fault.
explanation: The rhyme answers an accusation before it grows: maintaining oneself is not in itself a fault. The dictionary explains “feeding the belly” as supporting one’s life. In an ordinary conversation, the line can defend necessary work against snobbery about its status. That reading concerns the dignity of earning a living, not permission to harm others for gain. The short source supplies no trade, worker or occasion, so a particular occupation belongs to an illustrative example rather than to the saying’s documented history.
meaning_odia: ପେଟ ପୋଷିବାର ଅର୍ଥ ଅଭିଧାନରେ ନିଜର ଜୀବିକା ଚଳାଇବା। “ପୋଷ” ଓ “ଦୋଷ”ର ମେଳରେ ଜୀବିକାର ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ପାଇଁ ଛୋଟ ଏକ ସମର୍ଥନ ମିଳେ। କାମଟିକୁ ହୀନ ଭାବି କେହି ହସିଲେ, ନିଜ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ନିଜେ ଚଳାଇବାରେ ଲାଜ କାହିଁକି ବୋଲି ଏହା କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ। ଆମର ଏହି ପଢ଼ା ଜୀବିକାର ସମ୍ମାନକୁ ନେଇ; ଲାଭ ପାଇଁ ଅନ୍ୟର କ୍ଷତି କରିବାକୁ ସମର୍ଥନ କରେନାହିଁ।
english_summary: Earning one’s living is not itself something to be ashamed of.
odia_summary: ନିଜ ଜୀବିକା ଚଳାଇବାରେ ଲଜ୍ଜା ବା ଦୋଷ ନାହିଁ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: A student is embarrassed that acquaintances have seen her selling repaired furniture to support her studies. Her aunt quotes the saying, affirming the work rather than measuring its social prestige.
cultural_context: Livelihood is the explicit lexical sense. Dignity against occupational snobbery is editorial application, not a named movement, historical event or licence for wrongdoing.
